existing.description: The SUSS Research Scholarship supports applicants who have demonstrated academic excellence in social sciences and whose proposed research aligns with SUSS's research focus and faculty expertise. It is tenable for up to four years for PhD programmes and two years for the Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences. For full-time students it covers tuition fees excluding annual miscellaneous fees and pays a monthly stipend ranging from S$2,900 for an international MRES student to S$4,300 for a Singapore Citizen PhD student, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens; part-time students receive tuition fee coverage only. Selection is by merit during the programme admissions interview, followed by a panel interview for nominated applicants.
eligibility: Applicant seeking admission to one of the three eligible SUSS postgraduate programmes (PhD, PhD Gerontology, or Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences)
At least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree from a reputable university or equivalent qualifications
Demonstrated academic excellence in social sciences
Proposed research aligned with the research focus of SUSS and the expertise of SUSS faculty
Topics should relate to SUSS's Research Focus
Proposals relevant to the social services sector, with a clearly identified industry collaborator and likely cash and/or in-kind industry support, are prioritised
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants seeking admission to one of three SUSS postgraduate programmes - the Doctor of Philosophy (Office of Graduate Studies), the Doctor of Philosophy (Gerontology) (S R Nathan School of Human Development) or the Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences (School of Humanities and Behavioural Sciences) - who hold at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree from a reputable university or equivalent. Proposals relevant to the social services sector with a clearly identified industry collaborator and likely cash or in-kind industry support are prioritised, and topics should relate to SUSS's Research Focus.
benefits: Full-time: tuition fees (excluding annual miscellaneous fees) plus a monthly stipend
Part-time: tuition fee only (excluding annual miscellaneous fees)
Monthly stipend for PhD: S$4,300 Singapore Citizen, S$3,900 Permanent Resident, S$3,500 International Student
Monthly stipend for Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences: S$3,800 Singapore Citizen, S$3,000 Permanent Resident, S$2,900 International Student
CPF contributions are given on top of the stipend amounts for Singapore Citizens
International students on scholarship gain eligibility for the government tuition subsidy, which is otherwise unavailable to them
coverage: Tuition fees (excluding annual miscellaneous fees) for full-time students
Tuition fee only (excluding annual miscellaneous fees) for part-time students
documents: Research proposal aligned to SUSS's Research Focus
Evidence of at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree or equivalent
Evidence of academic excellence in social sciences
application_method: Apply for admission to one of the three eligible SUSS postgraduate programmes
Be evaluated on merit during the programme's admissions interview
If nominated, receive an email invitation to attend a panel interview for the scholarship
existing.selection_notes: Eligible applicants are evaluated on a merit basis during their admissions interviews; nominated applicants are invited by email to a panel interview for the scholarship. The decision of the SUSS Student Awards Committee is final and binding, no reasons are given for non-selection, and no appeals are entertained.
existing.best_fit: Strong social science applicants with a 2nd Upper Class Honours degree or equivalent applying to the SUSS PhD, PhD (Gerontology) or Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences, with a research topic aligned to SUSS's research focus.
existing.notes: This is distinct from the separate SUSS PhD Scholarship, which is for full-time PhD study only and also covers miscellaneous fees. International students on the Research Scholarship must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP) requirement and receive no remuneration for GAP hours. A government tuition subsidy is available to eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, and International Students are eligible for the subsidy only if awarded this scholarship.
existing.duration: A maximum of four years for PhD programmes and two years for the master programme
existing.application_period: Through admission to one of the three eligible SUSS postgraduate programmes; shortlisting and nomination happen during the admissions interview process
existing.deadline_display: SUSS publishes no standalone scholarship deadline for this award. It states that 'Eligible applicants to the three programmes will be evaluated on a merit basis during their admissions interviews. Potential applicants for the scholarship will be identified and nominated as part of the interview process', so the timing follows each programme's admissions cycle.
existing.program_type: Research scholarship for PhD and Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences
